title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, a representative validator-trace excerpt, quantitative analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models requires reliable mechanisms to avoid harmful, silent, or wrong-but-plausible actions. A common operational pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a generator (LLM) proposes a candidate configuration or plan, a deterministic validator mechanically checks correctness and policy constraints, and, when necessary, a repair module synthesizes corrected candidates or triggers human review. Prior demonstrations of GVR-like architectures in code and systems motivate their adoption in NetOps, but systematic, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive usefulness for end-to-end guarded success are scarce [1].

We preregistered study AC-2026-03 with a paired design that isolates the effect of downstream validator-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task the generator produced a single initial candidate that was reused by both the baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator+repair permitted) conditions. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise downstream from validator-triggered repair, not from independent generator sampling. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (H1) expected that a multidimensional validator-metric suite would explain more variance in end-to-end success than a single verifier pass rate. Our main contribution here is a fully preregistered, artifact-archived experiment and an exact, transparent report of a degenerate confirmatory outcome (ceiling) with concrete, artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up designs that can measure validator utility.
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and closed-loop verifier architectures have been proposed and evaluated in code and system domains to reduce stochastic generator error and to enable deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Recent NetOps and AIOps benchmark efforts document substantive failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate insertion of verifier layers [2],[3]. System and prototype reports propose self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. Broader surveys of LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps discuss adaptation and verification trade-offs and motivate metricized evaluation of verification cost versus nominal correctness [5].

These works collectively motivate a measurement focus on validator soundness and operational impact but do not provide a standardized, empirically estimable validator-metric suite for NetOps GVR flows. Our preregistered study was designed to begin filling that measurement gap under strict preregistration and archived-execution practices; when interpreted against the cited literature we treat prior demonstrations as architectural and motivational rather than as establishing empirical coverage for NetOps validators (we do not extrapolate beyond what the cited records support).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered elements: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini via provider bundle 'openai_responses'; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false (explicit). The preregistration included a power plan targeting detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power and bootstrap stability checks (1,000 resamples recommended for planning; actual analysis used 10,000 resamples as specified in the analysis executor). The preregistered primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the primary confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were drawn deterministically from a synthetic bank produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty levels labelled 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task specifies: an initial_state, an expected_final_state, a compact intent, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. These constraints ensure each task is an executable intent→configuration mapping with mechanistic checks a deterministic validator can enforce. Task selection followed a preregistered deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1) and contamination/exclusion rules (duplicate SHA-256 exclusion and semantic-similarity exclusion with embedding cosine threshold > 0.95). The execution bundle records task_manifest.jsonl and representative task entries (see archive). No contamination exclusions occurred in this run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model and sampling configuration. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Important artifact-grounded note: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). The preregistration and manuscript explicitly state that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; it is a recorded configuration field and provider-side sampling variability may still exist. The adapter's provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with exactly one shared initial generation per task.

Validator, scoring, and primary outcome. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and remediation artifacts when repairs are applied. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call when validator rejected a candidate; repairs would be recorded in repair_provider_trace fields and repair_applied toggled accordingly.

Execution, exclusions, and missingness controls. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). Missingness plan specified complete-pair analysis with sensitivity checks. The execution manifest shows completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200. No preregistered exclusion rules were triggered; the analysis bundle includes complete contamination and missingness summaries (analysis/missingness_summary.csv, analysis/contamination_summary.csv). All raw responses, validator traces, provider-call traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and referenced in the manuscript evidence bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No contamination exclusions or near-duplicate exclusions occurred.

Primary confirmatory result. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Summaries from analysis/condition_summary.csv: baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. The exact numeric analysis records are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and match the reported values.

Representative validator-trace excerpt. To illustrate validator semantics and why no repairs were triggered, we present a compact artifact-grounded excerpt from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (representative pair). Key fields (verbatim values from the archived artifact):
  - pair_id: pair-000004
  - normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  - parsed_command_count: 4
  - required_command_count: 4
  - observed_touched_field_count: 3
  - valid: true
  - repair_applied: false
  - validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  - validator_version: 5.0

For this exemplar the parsed/required command counts match, no violation codes were emitted, and the validator did not request repair. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode.

Diagnostic interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical initial candidate per pair; therefore any paired difference could only arise from deterministic validator-triggered repair. The degenerate all-valid outcome has three interlinked artifact-grounded determinants visible in the archived data: (1) the synthetic generator produced candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic constraints for the recorded generation seeds and prereduced task complexity as encoded by the generator; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) removed generator-variability as a source of disagreements; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but may not detect subtle semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure yet incorrect-by-intent). Together these factors explain why no repairs occurred and the confirmatory test could not detect the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement target.

Secondary analyses and exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN estimates are degenerate (no observed false positives or false negatives). Detection-latency and repair-invocation distributions are uninformative because repair_applied = false for all episodes. The execution bundle nevertheless contains full per-episode validator traces and raw responses (execution/raw_results.jsonl) to support reanalysis under alternative scoring or injected-fault conditions.
sections.discussion:
Inferential consequences. The preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics is well suited to isolate validator-triggered repair effects, but it also concentrates risk of a single-sample ceiling when the generator and validator align. The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted detection of a 10-percentage-point paired improvement). With baseline success = 1.0 the paired estimator has zero variance and the McNemar test and bootstrap CI are degenerate; no statistical procedure can detect an improvement that cannot occur in the observed data.

Operational interpretation and validator scope. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) provides reliable mechanistic intent-constraint checks recorded as parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flags. However, artifact-grounded evidence in this run shows that being correct-by-structure (validator.valid = true) does not guarantee semantic intent alignment under human operator expectations. That limitation is intrinsic to mechanistic validators that do not have external intent models or operator-feedback signals. Our results therefore do not indicate that validators are unnecessary: they prevented acceptance of invalid syntactic or structural candidates in other contexts, but in this particular synthetic bank and sampling regime there were zero detectable mechanical defects to catch.

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments. Based on archived execution artifacts and preregistered design infrastructure, we present concrete, reproducible next-step experiment prescriptions that would create measurable baseline failure prevalence and permit estimation of validator FP/FN and repair utility:
  1) Fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically inject a controlled set of faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). This creates measurable baseline invalidity and allows the guarded condition to demonstrate repair benefit. The execution bundle already supports deterministic task replacement and contamination checks to implement this arm without manual intervention.
  2) Multi-sample stochastic generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task (with independent sampling seeds recorded). Allow the guarded pipeline to accept any validator-approved candidate among the k draws or to perform repair; this reveals generator variability and creates opportunities for the validator to reject some draws and cause repair.
  3) Multi-validator comparison and model diversity: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family. Comparing validator coverage across implementations will quantify sensitivity to validator design choices and test external validity beyond the single validator used here.
Each prescription is directly supported by the archived artifacts and adapter semantics (hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Implementing these preregistered arms would produce non-degenerate data suitable for estimating FP/FN, detection latency, repair utility, and predictive R^2 against an operational-impact proxy as originally planned.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate choice intentionally isolates downstream effects but introduced single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: binary validator.valid maps to mechanistic correctness but may fail to capture semantic intent misalignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model (gpt-5-mini), and a single deterministic validator limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks and alternative model families. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance in the primary estimand; hence inferential conclusions about validator benefit are not possible from this execution alone. These limitations are explicitly recorded in the execution and analysis artifacts and motivate the artifact-grounded follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. This result is artifact-grounded and reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and provide concrete, preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. The artifacts and analysis logs are archived in the execution bundle for community reanalysis and for use as the basis of follow-up preregistered experiments that can resolve the open measurement questions identified here.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
